steps.tx: **NTRK gene fusions** involving NTRK1, NTRK2, NTRK3 encode oncogenic chimeric TRK kinases sensitive to selective **TRK inhibitors** larotrectinib and entrectinib across all histologies. These genomic rearrangements fuse the 3-prime kinase domain of NTRK with 5-prime upstream partners, resulting in ligand-independent constitutive tyrosine kinase signalling driving cellular proliferation and survival across diverse paediatric and adult solid malignancies.

nodes.label: Loss of MMR (MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2)

steps.tx: The model shows a chimeric **TRK kinase** created by an **NTRK fusion** firing without normal ligand control. **Larotrectinib** occupies the kinase domain and denies ATP entry. That single blockade silences **downstream signaling** through growth and survival cascades, which is why one drug works across many tumour types sharing the fusion.
steps.say: Some cancers are driven by NTRK gene fusions that join a partner gene to the TRK kinase, leaving it permanently switched on. Larotrectinib fits into the kinase pocket and blocks energy use, so growth signals stop. This diagram shows the drug in place with downstream paths turned off. Because the target is the fusion itself, benefit applies regardless of where the tumour started.

vis.alt: Molecular model shows larotrectinib bound in an active NTRK fusion kinase with downstream signaling switched off.
vis.caption: Model shows larotrectinib silencing an NTRK fusion kinase. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: NTRK gene fusions are uncommon across tumour types, yet they can be **actionable** because a single **tropomyosin receptor kinase** pathway drives growth. Matching a **targeted therapy** to the fusion, rather than to the organ of origin, is the core idea of tissue agnostic practice. Mismatch repair deficiency and high **microsatellite instability** signal a different route, where **immune checkpoint inhibitors** are often considered early.

vis.caption: Tissue-agnostic therapy: biomarker dictates treatment, not organ of origin

steps.tx: MSI-H and **mismatch repair-deficient** dMMR solid tumours demonstrate profound, durable responsiveness to immune **checkpoint inhibitors** regardless of anatomical origin. Defective mismatch repair genes MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, and PMS2 lead to thousands of somatic frameshift mutations, producing immunogenic neoantigens that induce robust cytotoxic T-cell recruitment and programmed death-1 axis vulnerability.

rows: Validated by FoundationOne CDx NGS assay
Statistically significant benefit across diverse histologies
Durable responses in anal, biliary, cervical, and vulvar cancers
Gliomas and uveal melanoma show poor response
Low baseline TIL infiltration despite high mutational burden

steps.tx: High **tumour mutational burden** defined as 10 or more mutations per megabase serves as a tumour-agnostic **predictive biomarker** for pembrolizumab monotherapy. In the KEYNOTE-158 trial, patients with TMB-high status achieved an objective response rate of 29% compared to 6% in non-TMB-high tumours, reflecting heightened neoantigen display that triggers potent endogenous antitumour T-lymphocyte immunity.

left.title: Larotrectinib
points: Highly selective pan-TRK inhibitor (TRKA, TRKB, TRKC)
Systemic ORR 75% to 79% in TRK-fusion cancers
Approved across all ages including infants and children
Adverse effects: fatigue, elevated AST/ALT, neurotoxicity

right.title: Entrectinib
points: Potent inhibitor of TRKA/B/C, ROS1, and ALK
High blood-brain barrier penetration with intracranial activity
Approved for NTRK fusion-positive tumours and ROS1+ NSCLC
Adverse effects: dysgeusia, weight gain, cognitive changes

steps.tx: **BRAF V600E** mutation combination therapy with dabrafenib and trametinib carries **tissue-agnostic** approval for all advanced solid tumours lacking satisfactory alternative options. BRAF V600E causes constitutive monomeric activation of downstream MEK and ERK kinases, and dual pathway blockade with dabrafenib and trametinib prevents paradoxical MAPK reactivation and delays emergence of acquired resistance.

nodes.label: Steric Clash & Loss of First-Line Binding

steps.tx: **RET gene fusions** and activating RET mutations across diverse solid tumours respond to highly **selective RET inhibitors** selpercatinib and pralsetinib. In the LIBRETTO-001 and ARROW trials, these ATP-competitive inhibitors demonstrated dramatic, durable objective responses exceeding 60% with marked intracranial central nervous system penetration, irrespective of whether the tumour originated in the lung, thyroid, colon, or breast.

Any solid tumour with V600E post-progression

steps.tx: HER2-directed antibody-drug conjugate **trastuzumab deruxtecan** is approved tumour-agnostically for pretreated unresectable or metastatic **HER2 IHC 3+** solid tumours. Based on the pan-tumour DESTINY-PanTumor02 study, trastuzumab deruxtecan demonstrated confirmed objective response rates of 51% across biliary, bladder, cervical, endometrial, ovarian, and other pretreated HER2-positive non-breast malignancies.

left.title: Selpercatinib (LOXO-292)
points: Highly selective oral RET kinase inhibitor
Tissue-agnostic approval for RET fusion-positive solid tumours
Potent central nervous system penetration (> 80% intracranial ORR)
Active against RET gatekeeper V804M/L resistance mutations

right.title: Pralsetinib (BLU-667)
points: Selective RET inhibitor targeting oncogenic RET fusions
Approved in RET fusion-positive NSCLC and thyroid cancers
High potency against multiple RET partner rearrangements
Adverse events include hypertension, neutropenia, pneumonitis

steps.tx: **Molecular tumour boards** integrate comprehensive **genomic sequencing** data with clinical trials, evaluating variant pathogenicity according to AMP/ASCO/CAP tier criteria. Multidisciplinary discussion balances variant allele frequencies, co-occurring resistance alterations, and level of actionability, translating complex next-generation sequencing assays into actionable, off-label, or investigational basket trial matches for refractory cancer patients.

rows: Single targeted therapy tested across multiple distinct cancer histologies harboring the identical molecular alteration
VE-BASKET (vemurafenib in V600E); NAVIGATE (larotrectinib in TRK)
Multiple different targeted therapies evaluated within a single histology stratified by individual molecular sub-cohorts
Continuous rolling multi-arm design allowing entry and exit of therapies based on interim adaptive efficacy

steps.tx: Clonal versus **subclonal** driver status determines durable **targeted efficacy**: subclonal alterations demonstrate lower response rates due to outgrowth of negative tumour clones. Truncal mutations present in all malignant cells provide uniform vulnerability, whereas subclonal mutations present only in branch subclones inevitably lead to rapid therapeutic failure as wild-type cells expand under selective pressure.
